messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT: HIGH severity - customer=AcadiaCorp (privnet) affected. Symptom: egress NLB healthchecks failing -> instances marked unhealthy. Affected: dedicated-private-gw-nlb (us-west-2) | paging oncall-sre.
Sara R.: saw the page, joining. Any customer impact reported yet?
Mike L.: healthchecks 502/503 from the NLB targets. backend instances responding 200 when hit directly.
Raj P.: suspect SG or egress path. NLB -> NAT -> internet for healthcheck endpoint (third-party). If NAT returns 503 when concurrent conn hits limit, could mark targets unhealthy.
Emily S.: Acadia reported API errors and degraded inference latency ~5m ago. They're seeing 5xxs on calls routed via their private deployment.
Sara R.: ok starting triage. grabbing NLB logs and target health history. can someone check VPC Flow Logs for drops to the monitoring endpoint?
Mike L.: eyeballing flow logs now — outbound to monitoring endpoint 54.83.21.5 shows RSTs from nat-xx. Connection attempts succeed then reset after handshake.
Raj P.: quick config check: their tenant SG had a deny-all-outbound except to internal subnets earlier today for hardening. Could be blocking ephemeral healthcheck source port ranges.
Lina K.: (from acct) Acadia is on Dedicated Private plan and has a reserved pool. They're very sensitive to downtime. Keep them updated.
Sara R.: confirm: target instances respond OK locally. NLB health probe originates from NLB IPs and should hit instance port 8080. If instance returns OK, but NAT bounces probe back, health fails.
Mike L.: ran curl from one target to monitoring endpoint -> succeeds. curl from within the NAT gateway pod shows intermittent 502s. Looks like natgw capacity saturation + conntrack exhaustion.
Raj P.: mitigation options: 1) increase NAT GW throughput (add extra natgw) 2) add SG egress allowance for the monitoring endpoint so instances can be probed locally (bypass nat) 3) temporary reroute healthchecks to ALB inside VPC that hits instances directly.
Sara R.: fastest: update NLB healthcheck to probe a local health endpoint (127.0.0.1:9000/probe) that'll return from instance before egress. But need to ensure app exposes that. Can we flip probe to local /hc?
Mike L.: instance already exposes /internal-health on 9000. NLB currently set to 8080. Changing probes on production NLB could cause churn; but this is targeted customer private NLB so ok with careful step.
Jordan T.: I'll prepare the change. Plan: 1) set NLB healthcheck path -> /internal-health on port 9000, interval 10s, threshold 2 2) monitor target healthy 3) rollback if errors.
Emily S.: I'll draft customer update: "We're investigating egress healthcheck failures affecting your private gateway. Temporary healthcheck reroute underway to stabilize traffic — no config changes required on your side."
Sara R.: execute now. Jordan, apply changes and push. Callout: keep connection draining to avoid in-flight requests failure.
(2m later) Jordan T.: applied healthcheck switch. Watching targets...
Mike L.: targets moved to healthy within 25s. NLB shows 100% healthy. Observability: backend 5xxs drop to baseline.
Sara R.: nice. Now follow-ups: 1) provision extra NAT GW or shift to managed shared NAT for this tenant 2) increase conntrack table on NAT instance if used 3) submit runbook update for private deployments to include local probe option.
Raj P.: raising a ticket to infra to add one additional nat gateway in customer VPC. tagging eng-infra.
Lina K.: thanks — I'll inform Acadia that we've stabilized and plan changes; request permission for infra work during maintenance window.
Emily S.: customer message sent: "Temporary healthcheck reroute implemented; this stabilized requests. We're coordinating long-term fix with an infra update and will follow up with timeline."
Sara R.: great. closing loop: incident severity -> reduced to MED until NAT capacity fix is scheduled. leaving thread open for infra ETA. :white_check_mark:
